subject: Metrosphere renewal discussion — continuity proposal & benchmark packet
messages:
From: Jules Hammond <jules@metrosphere.io>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T16:12:00Z
Subject: Looking ahead to renewal — benchmarking and constraints

Hi Olga,

Our current term with Redwood comes up in February and procurement has signaled they want to run a focused vendor comparison this quarter. The external partner is pushing hard on price-per-token and is promising a 20-30% unit cost reduction, but we're concerned about latency and enterprise features (SLA, audit logs).

Can you share a concise baseline we can use in our bakeoff? Specifically: 95th percentile generation latency at our typical payloads, cost per 1M tokens at both on-demand and committed rates, and whether dedicated pools / reserved capacity would change those numbers materially.

Attached our RFP for context. We'd like a short call next week to agree on a mutual action plan — ideally we can get an operational benchmark and a continuity proposal to share with procurement and engineering.

Thanks,
Jules Hammond
Director of Platform Engineering
Metrosphere

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Looking ahead to renewal — benchmarking and constraints

Thanks Jules — appreciate the heads-up and the RFP.

Looping in Marcus (Solutions) and Priyom (SE) so we can move quickly. High-level plan from our side:
- Run a targeted benchmark against a representative subset of your traffic (we'll need 1-2 sample prompts per flow and guidance on concurrency).
- Produce a short packet (latency percentiles, cost simulators for on-demand vs committed, and recommended reserved capacity).
- Put together a continuity proposal: term options (12 vs 24 months), step-up capacity schedule, and a commercial outline including credits for migration work.

Can you share:
1) Typical prompt length distribution (p95 tokens).
2) Peak concurrent requests in a typical daily spike.
3) Any hard constraints: data residency, SOC2 evidence, or SLA thresholds that must be in the contract.

We can do a 30-min sync Wed or Thu next week — propose Wed 10/06 09:00-09:30 PT or Thu 10/07 11:00-11:30 PT.

Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jules Hammond <jules@metrosphere.io>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-26T18:20:00Z
Subject: Metrosphere targeted benchmark & operational findings

Jules — following our run against the sample workload (thanks for the traces), please find the summarized results attached along with a small latency CSV. High level:

- Latency (generation, single-stream, p95): 290ms at baseline config (gpt-analog-std), 230ms with KV-prefix caching and optimized batching.
- Cost: on-demand equivalent ~ $18 / 1M tokens (baseline). Committed reserved pool reduces unit cost to ~$13 / 1M tokens at the reservation levels we modeled.
- Peak concurrency: at your reported p99 spike (~480 concurrent streams) we see queuing start to appear on shared hosted nodes; reserving a dedicated pool sized for that peak eliminates queuing and reduces p95 by ~40ms.

Operational recommendations:
- Reserved Capacity: 4x A100-equivalent slots (auto-burst policy for 10% headroom).
- Cache + batching: enable prefix KV cache for chat flows (our run showed ~20% token reduction and lower latency tail).
- Rollout: canary in one region for 2 weeks then traffic split 50/50 for next 2 weeks.

Commercial starter offer (for discussion):
- 12-month extension: 10% off list rates on committed units + one-time $50,000 professional services credit for migration/ops tuning.
- 24-month extension: 16% off list + $85,000 PS credit + guaranteed latency SLA (p95 < 350ms on reserved pool).

I've attached: metrosphere_q3-inference-benchmarks.pdf (full deck) and latency-report-1026.csv (raw measures). We'll draft an amendment outlining the step-up schedule and the draft SLA for legal to digest.

-marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

- SLA language (p95 latency objective) and monitoring hooks for token-level billing transparency.

From: Leah Kim <leah.kim@metrosphere.io>

Date: 2026-11-08T15:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft amendment & proposal for continuity — Metrosphere (DEAL-78321)

Olga / team — thanks for the packet and the draft amendment. Procurement + legal reviewed and we have a short list of asks before we can route to signature: 
1) Explicit SLA remedy language for sustained p95 breaches (we need clarity on credits calculation).
2) Data residency confirmation for EU customer records and a one-page list of audit artifacts (SOC2 links).
3) A 90-day break clause at month 12 if competitive performance materially exceeds the committed pool (procurement wants a safety valve).

All of these are negotiable; the team liked the committed-capacity approach and the PS credit. Attaching our procurement questions for your legal team to review. If we can get a clean pass on the SLA language and a written note on data residency, procurement is ready to move legal review forward and target signature by 2026-11-22.

Leah Kim
Senior Procurement Manager
Metrosphere
